sentences.cn_text: 随着14世纪佛罗伦萨被称为文艺复兴的创造力迸发，现代世界开始脱离其曾经熟知的一切。
sentences.en_text: Following the explosion of creativity in Florence during the 14th century Known as the Renaissance, the modem world saw a departure from what it had once known.

sentences.cn_text: 它不再信奉上帝和罗马天主教会的权威，转而倾向于一种更加人文主义的存在方式。
sentences.en_text: It turned from God and the authority of the Roman Catholic Church and instead favoured a more humanistic approach to being.

sentences.cn_text: 文艺复兴思想在整个欧洲传播开来，一直延续到17世纪，艺术和科学在那些更具逻辑倾向的人群中呈现出异常繁荣的景象。
sentences.en_text: Renaissance ideas had spread throughout Europe well into the 17th century, with the arts and sciences flourishing extraordinarily among those with a more logical disposition.

sentences.cn_text: 随着教会的教义和思维方式被文艺复兴所取代，中世纪与现代时期之间的鸿沟得以弥合，从而通向了新的、未经探索的知识领域。
sentences.en_text: With the Church’s teachings and ways of thinking being eclipsed by the Renaissance, the gap between the Medieval and modern periods had been bridged, leading to new and unexplored intellectual territories.

sentences.cn_text: 在文艺复兴时期,尼古拉·哥白尼、约翰内斯·开普勒和伽利略·伽利莱等伟大的思想家展示了科学研究和发现的力量。
sentences.en_text: During the Renaissance, the great minds of Nicolaus Copernicus, Johannes Kepler and Galileo Galilei demonstrated the power of scientific study and discovery.

sentences.cn_text: 在他们每次揭示真相之前，当时的许多思想家仍秉持更为古老的思维方式，包括认为地球位于宇宙中心的地心说。
sentences.en_text: Before each of their revelations, many thinkers at the time had sustained more ancient ways of thinking, including the geocentric view that the Earth was at the centre of our universe.

sentences.cn_text: 哥白尼在1543年提出理论，认为实际上我们所知的所有行星并非围绕地球旋转，而是围绕太阳旋转，这一体系后来由伽利略不惜代价予以支持。
sentences.en_text: Copernicus theorized in 1543 that in actual fact, all of the planets that we knew of revolved not around the Earth, but the Sun, a system that was later upheld by Galileo at his own expense.

sentences.cn_text: 在科学与宗教思想高度紧张的时期提出这样的理论被斥为异端，任何继续传播这些「谎言」的异端分子都将受到监禁甚至处死的惩罚。
sentences.en_text: Offering up such a theory during a time of high tension between scientific and religious minds was branded as heresy, and any such heretics that continued to spread these lies were to be punished by imprisonment or even death.

sentences.cn_text: 尽管教会试图压制这一代新的逻辑学家和理性主义者，但关于宇宙如何运行的更多解释正以人们无法再忽视的速度涌现。
sentences.en_text: Despite attempts by the Church to suppress this new generation of logicians and rationalists, more explanations for how the universe functioned were being made at a rate that the people could no longer ignore.

sentences.cn_text: 正是伴随这些伟大的发现，一种建立在理性基础上的新型哲学诞生了。
sentences.en_text: It was with these great revelations that a new kind of philosophy founded in reason was born.

sentences.cn_text: 教会长期坚守的教条正在关于真理的伟大较量中败给理性主义者和科学家。
sentences.en_text: The Church’s long-standing dogma was losing the great battle for truth to rationalists and scientists.

sentences.cn_text: 这一事实本身体现了17世纪大部分时期席卷欧洲的新思维方式。
sentences.en_text: This very fact embodied the new ways of thinking that swept through Europe during most of the 17th century.

sentences.cn_text: 随着许多人承担起将理性和科学哲学融入世界的使命，文艺复兴结束了，一个新的时代——理性时代——到来了。
sentences.en_text: As many took on the duty of trying to integrate reasoning and scientific philosophies into the world, the Renaissance was over and it was time for a new era — the Age of Reason.

sentences.cn_text: 17世纪和18世纪是充满剧变和好奇心的时代。
sentences.en_text: The 17th and 18th centuries were times of radical change and curiosity.

sentences.cn_text: 科学方法、还原论以及对教会理念的质疑应当受到鼓励，自由、宽容和进步的思想也应如此。
sentences.en_text: Scientific method, reductionism and the questioning of Church ideals was to be encouraged, as were ideas of liberty, tolerance and progress.

sentences.cn_text: 这些寻求知识并理解我们已知信息的行为被拉丁短语「sapere aude」即「敢于求知」所概括，这一短语由伊曼努尔·康德在其论文《何谓启蒙》中使用。
sentences.en_text: Such actions to seek knowledge and to understand what information we already knew were captured by the Latin phrase “sapere aude” or “dare to know”, after Immanuel Kant used it in his essay “An Answer to the Question: What is Enlightenment?”.

sentences.cn_text: 伟大思想家的使命和责任是去探求真理，他们相信真理根植于知识之中。
sentences.en_text: It was the purpose and responsibility of great minds to go forth and seek out the truth, which they believed to be founded in knowledge.
